scopeNote: Rawai, Nai Harn, Promthep and Sai Yuan first (18 places near the Rawai villa), then Chalong, Kata, Kata Noi, Karon, Cape Panwa and Ao Yon; local Thai, seafood, pork, grills, bakeries and a few special dinners.

items.name: Rawai Seafood Market
items.nameThai: ตลาดทะเลสด หาดราไวย์
items.gmapsQuery: Rawai Seafood Market, Wiset Road, Rawai, Phuket
items.priceText: Cooking fee about 100 THB per kg, or 50-100 THB per dish at some shops; large prawns up to 1,500 THB per kg (Phuket 101, Sep 2026). One Google reviewer paid 1,500 THB for 5.7 kg of seafood, plus about 100 THB per kg to cook it (quoted on Wanderlog, 2026).
dishes: Steamed blue crab with chilli-lime dip
Whole fish fried with garlic or steamed with lime
items.praise: Phuket 101 (Sep 2026) names the cook-shops behind the stalls: Mook Manee is the biggest and the only one in the Michelin Guide; Khun Pha Seafood charges per dish and reviewers rate its cooking and value; Fish Bar is smaller and quieter; Chay Lay, at the far end, will fetch items from the market for you. An r/phuket comment: buy at the market and have Mook Manee cook it, 'simply the best place to go'.
items.watchOut: Agree the price per kg before they bag it, and watch the scale. Ask how the cooking fee works (per kg or per dish) before you hand over the bag. Prices are no longer cheap.
items.description: A strip of fish stalls by Rawai Pier with cook-shops across the road. You buy fish, prawns, crab or lobster by weight and a restaurant cooks it the way you ask.
items.bestTime: 18:00-19:00 for dinner. Late morning is quietest.
tips: For 8 people, Mook Manee has the most space; Khun Pha charges per dish, which is easier to plan.
Bring cash for the stalls.
For a quieter meal with its own menu, walk 300 m to Salaloy.
items.verification: Google Maps 27 Oct 2026: 4.4, open, pin on Wiset Road. Phuket 101 market page (updated 21 Sep 2026) for the cook-shops and fees. Wanderlog (Oct 2026): Google 4,719 reviews, Tripadvisor 4.2 from 314.

items.name: Mook Manee
items.nameThai: มุขมณี ซีฟู้ด
items.gmapsQuery: Mook Manee Seafood, 1120 Wiset Road, Rawai, Phuket

otherRatings.note: top of the Rawai list on Wongnai

items.priceText: Cheese-baked scallops 400 THB (Phuket 101, Sep 2026). Live lobster 800-1,200 THB each, grilled tiger prawns 250 THB each, crab curry 500-700 THB (Phuket 101 seafood guide, Jul 2026).
dishes: Stir-fried clams with chilli paste (nam prik pao)
items.praise: The Michelin inspector picks the stir-fried clams with chilli paste and the seats over the market. Phuket 101 (Sep 2026) calls it the largest and busiest restaurant at the market, more commercial than the older places, with many Asian tour groups.
items.watchOut: Busy with tour groups at peak times. Seafood is sold by weight, so check the price before it is cooked.
items.description: The biggest restaurant at the Rawai market, with live seafood tanks and a covered terrace that seats hundreds. You can order from the menu or bring seafood bought at the stalls.
items.bestTime: Early dinner before 18:30, or a late lunch.
tips: Call ahead for a table for 8: 081 719 4880 (Michelin listing).
Ask for a table that looks over the market and the boats.
items.verification: Google Maps 27 Oct 2026: 4.2, open 11:30-22:00, pin by the market. Michelin page read 27 Oct 2026 (listed, no star or Bib; it was a Bib Gourmand in 2023). Phuket 101 page updated 21 Sep 2026.

items.name: Salaloy Seafood
items.nameThai: ร้านอาหาร ศาลาลอย
items.gmapsQuery: Salaloy Seafood Restaurant, 52/2 Wiset Road, Rawai, Phuket
items.priceText: Grilled squid 150-250 THB by size, tom yum goong 180 THB, crab fried rice 150 THB; about 300-400 THB per person (Phuket 101, Jul 2026).
dishes: Moo sam chan yang: grilled pork belly
Kaeng som: sour fish curry with vegetables
items.praise: Michelin (2023 article) wrote that the seafood is so fresh 'you'd think it swam up just to fill your order'. Phuket 101 (Oct 2026) lists it among Phuket's best local restaurants and recommends the charcoal-grilled prawns and grilled squid; it is busy at both lunch and dinner.
items.watchOut: Closed on Thursdays. Some seafood runs out late in the day. Phuket 101 still calls it Michelin-listed, but its Michelin page is gone and it is not in the 2026 selection.
items.description: Long-running Thai seafood restaurant on Rawai Beach. The kitchen is on one side of the road and the best tables are under tall trees by the water on the other.
items.bestTime: Arrive before 12:30 for lunch or before 18:30 for dinner.
tips: Add the grilled pork belly to the seafood order.
Ask for a table on the sea side of the road.
Bring cash.
items.verification: Google Maps 27 Oct 2026: 4.3, open 11:30-21:00. Phuket 101 lists (Jul and Oct 2026) for prices, dishes and the Thursday closing. Michelin restaurant page returned 404 on 27 Oct 2026, so it has left the guide.

items.name: Baan Rimlay
items.nameThai: ร้านอาหารบ้านริมเล
items.gmapsQuery: Ban Rimlay Restaurant, 44 Wiset Road, Rawai, Phuket
items.priceText: Most diners spend 200-500 THB per person; there is no printed price list for fish by weight (Phuket 101, Sep 2026).
items.praise: Phuket 101 (Sep 2026): a small, simple dining room built over the water a few steps from Rawai Pier, popular with locals; Thai-language reviews often praise the tamarind prawns and seafood salads.
items.watchOut: Ask the price before fish is weighed. Rawai faces east, so there is no sunset here.
items.description: Small open-sided restaurant over the water next to Rawai Pier, with wooden tables under big trees. Simple Thai seafood at local prices.
items.bestTime: Lunch, or dinner at high tide.
tips: A quieter, cheaper choice than the market restaurants next door.
items.verification: Google Maps 27 Oct 2026: 4.3, open, pin at 44 Wiset Road. Phuket 101 page updated 21 Sep 2026.

items.name: Nikita's Beach Restaurant
items.gmapsQuery: Nikita's Beach Restaurant, 44/1 Wiset Road, Rawai, Phuket
items.priceText: No menu prices found. Phuket 101 (Oct 2026) calls prices excellent for the location.
items.praise: A long-running favourite of expats and returning visitors. Phuket 101 (Oct 2026) says the Thai food and seafood are good and prices are excellent for the spot; its older review adds that it is 'probably not as good as it used to be', but still worth a stop.
items.watchOut: Reliable rather than special; the setting under the trees is the main draw.
items.description: Open-air restaurant under big trees at the south end of Rawai Beach, with Thai food, seafood and wood-fired pizza. Easy for a mixed group.
tips: Good when some of the group want pizza and others want Thai food.
items.verification: Google Maps 27 Oct 2026: 4.3, open 10:00-23:00. Phuket 101 Nai Harn list (updated 12 Oct 2026). Wanderlog (Oct 2026) for the Tripadvisor count.

items.watchOut: We found little recent detail on the main dishes. Go for the mango sticky rice and a simple meal.
items.description: Family-run Thai restaurant by the water at the south end of Rawai Beach, known for its mango sticky rice.

Lunch is usually walk-in.

Moo kua kluea: pork belly fried with salt
items.praise: Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026. The inspector names the stuffed mackerel, squid with black ink and crab rolls. Phuket 101 (Oct 2026) calls it 'a proper Thai dining experience the way locals enjoy it' and says to count the cars in the car park.
items.watchOut: Closed on the 15th of every month (on your trip: Fri 15 Jan). No bookings, and weekend queues. Some huts have floor seating.
items.description: Southern Thai seafood in wooden huts over a mangrove canal, mostly Thai diners, with live seafood in tanks by the kitchen.
items.openText: Daily 10:00-21:00 (Google). Closed on the 15th of each month.
items.bestTime: Weekday lunch. On weekends arrive before 12:00.
tips: Order the salt-crusted fish first; it takes about 30 minutes.
Ask for a hut over the water; bigger huts have chairs.
The menu has photos, so you can point.

items.name: Kata Night Market (Taina)

Spread out and order from several stalls for the group.
